items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: You know I mean he’s an institution of himself, Elvin, and so is Art.

ctx.x: Well it’s like when they give you a piece of music say for instance. The composer may have put certain rhythms on there or certain voicings. Or like when I pass out bass parts, I say please don’t play that, this is just an idea. I am not a bass player, so please don’t play what I wrote, but this will just give you a general feel, now I want you to take it and do your thing with it. And the drums, same with the drums. You know you’ve got some guys who say, “I want you to play this” [scats]. I say man, please,…

goes, “Let me try it.” And he put this whole other beat on it and took it somewhere else. And my eyes, I said okay, the little light bulb went off, you know? How stupid I am trying to tell Art Blakey to play it kind of Elvinish. You know I mean he’s an institution of himself, Elvin, and so is Art. And you know if you’ve got Art, you take Art, you don’t want — you want Elvin [Jones], you go get Elvin.
That’s like telling Ali to box like Frasier.
